messages:
maria: Heads up — AcmeCorp reported that their Private deployment (VPC mode, behind customer LB + our ingress) intermittently fails SSO. They say it works from browser but API calls from their backend to our /v1/chat endpoint get 401s. Repro steps below.

maria: Relevant context: customer terminates TLS at their LB, does cookie->Bearer conversion with an auth-proxy, then forwards to our L7 gateway (Envoy + Istio). They claim Authorization header is set before the LB.

akash: can you paste the minimal repro?

maria: yes. curl against their LB (they gave us a test host):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted-token>" \
  -H "Host: acme-api.example" \
  https://acme-lb.test.example.net/v1/chat -sS -D -
```

maria: At the LB we see the header in logs: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` but our gateway returns 401.

timothy: do tcpdumps on the node in their VPC where our gateway is running show the header? If they terminate TLS at LB we won't see TLS, but between LB and our ingress it's plaintext TLS?

maria: They forward over plain HTTP (LB -> our ingress). I asked them to tcpdump and they sent this excerpt from the edge node (snip):

```
GET /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: acme-api.example
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: */*
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
X-Forwarded-For: 3.3.3.3

```

maria: But our gateway logs show the request without Authorization:

```
[2026-02-14T13:02:11Z] incoming request path=/v1/chat method=POST headers={host: acme-api.example, user-agent: curl/7.68.0}
```

akash: hmm. That smells like the LB or Istio/Envoy strip or rewrite the header OR a header mapping mismatch (e.g., LB puts X-Forwarded-Authorization). Ask them to dump raw bytes at the socket to confirm.

timothy: also check whether the LB converts to HTTP/2 to upstream — some proxies canonicalize header names or move them to metadata. Envoy http/2 path might move pseudoheaders around.

maria: They ran `nc` on the upstream and captured shows `authorization` (lowercase) instead of `Authorization`. Their gateway code only looks for capitalized `Authorization` (ugh).

maria: Example from their capture: `authorization: Bearer REDACTED`

akash: HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so our runtime should not care. But our header parsing or a custom filter might be doing a string match. Which component logs headers? Is that the application or the gateway?

maria: The log above is from our ingress (gateway service). Looks like the filter that extracts auth token expects header name `Authorization` exactly (we do have a TODO about normalizing).

sre-oncall: if the header name casing is the only issue, quick fix is to normalize header names in the filter. But need to be careful with other proxies — some set `x-forwarded-authorization` when doing auth conversions. Ask customer for that too.

maria: They also stated in one incident that sometimes our gateway sees `X-Auth-Token` instead of Authorization. They admit they have an old auth-proxy that sets `X-Auth-Token` in some code paths.

timothy: OK actionable list: 1) confirm whether header casing vs name mapping is the root cause, 2) check for X-Forwarded-Authorization or X-Auth-Token, 3) check if Istio external auth (ext-authz) is configured on their side and consuming the header before it reaches our filter.

maria: I asked them to curl with a custom header too:

```bash
curl -v -H "X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Authorization: " \
  https://acme-lb.test.example.net/v1/chat -sS -D -
```

maria: Their LB logs then show both headers, but our gateway still doesn't see X-Forwarded-Authorization.

akash: This is starting to look like header rewriting or hop-by-hop removal. Some LBs drop `Authorization` unless you enable pass-through (ALB has a setting), and some ingress controllers explicitly remove `Authorization` before internal routing. We should check Istio config: `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` or any Lua filters.

maria: I pulled the istio-proxy config from the affected node and found a Lua filter that strips sensitive headers for audit:

```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local hdr = request_handle:headers()
  hdr:remove("Authorization")
  hdr:remove("authorization")
end
```

maria: Customer admits they added that because they didn't want downstream services accidentally logging tokens. But that removes token before our gateway auth filter runs. Oops.

sre-oncall: there's the smoking gun. We need them to move that filter to run after our auth stage, or better: have the filter mask tokens rather than drop them. Eg replace value with "REDACTED-TRUNC".

timothy: short-term workaround: update our gateway to accept X-Auth-Token or X-Forwarded-Authorization as fallback. Long-term: update our ingestion docs to require Authorization to be forwarded and call out common misconfigs.

maria: I suggested the mask approach and gave them a patch snippet for the Lua filter to redact instead of remove. They tested and reported success (our gateway now sees `Authorization: REDACTED-TRUNC` — our filter then verifies presence and returns 401 if token missing, but at least we get deterministic behavior).

akash: please open a KB article — include common LB behaviors (ALB/NGINX/HAProxy), istio ext-authz ordering, and the redaction vs removal nuance. Also include a quick curl parity test using netcat on upstream to confirm header path.

maria: filing now. Also flagged an internal task to harden our auth filter: normalize header names, and accept common forwarded names as fallback. I'll create a small canary for the change.

sre-oncall: deploying canary today. @deploy-bot start canary roll for service=redwood-gateway tag=canary-auth-fallback 5m windows

deploy-bot: Canary started: redwood-gateway:canary-auth-fallback — monitoring for 5m.

maria: customer confirmed SSO issues resolved after redaction change. They'll keep the redaction in place until we ship the gateway fix.

timothy: follow-ups: 1) KB + support playbook, 2) gateway patch (normalize headers + fallback), 3) check our logs to ensure we don't log tokens after our change. 4) add a small test to integration that checks Authorization with mixed-case header name.

maria: thanks all. I'll update thread when KB + PR are ready.

akash: nice catch — thanks to the customer for sharing Lua snippet.

maria: any questions ping me.

sre-oncall: noted. marking incident resolved for now, will reopen if canary shows trouble.
